domain_restrictions: f is a total function from the Euclidean plane R^2 to the two-element set {red,green}
A,B,C,P,O are points of the Euclidean plane R^2
the hypothesis applies only to triples A,B,C that are noncollinear (hence distinct) so the circumcenter is uniquely defined in R^2
the circumcenter operation circ(A,B,C) is the unique intersection of perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC (uses Euclidean geometry)
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every function f: R^2 -> {red,green}, if for all points A,B,C in R^2 that are noncollinear and satisfy f(A)=f(B)=f(C) we have f(circumcenter(A,B,C)) = f(A), then there exists a color c in {red,green} such that for every point P in R^2, f(P)=c. Equivalently: ∀f [(∀A,B,C (noncollinear ∧ f(A)=f(B)=f(C) ⇒ f(circumcenter(A,B,C))=f(A))) ⇒ (∃c ∈ {red,green} ∀P f(P)=c)].
quantifier_order: forall f : R^2 -> {red,green} (consider any 2-coloring of the plane)
assume (hypothesis) forall A,B,C in R^2: if A,B,C are noncollinear and f(A)=f(B)=f(C) then f(circumcenter(A,B,C)) = f(A)
conclude: exists c in {red,green} such that forall P in R^2, f(P) = c

payload.theorem_nl: Suppose that each point in the plane is colored either red or green, subject to the following condition: For every three noncollinear points $A,B,C$ of the same color, the center of the circle passing through $A,B$ and $C$ is also this color. Prove that all points of the plane are the same color.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix a coloring f satisfying the hypothesis that the circumcenter of any noncollinear monochromatic triple has the same color. By Lemma L4, some color class contains a noncollinear triple; call the color c, and call the triple A,B,C. By Lemma L1, the color class S_c = {P : f(P)=c} is closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples from S_c. Since A,B,C are noncollinear points of S_c, Lemma L5 applies and yields S_c = R^2. Unwinding the definition of S_c, every point of the plane has color c. Therefore the coloring is constant, which is exactly the theorem.

steps.derives: There exists a color c in {red,green} and points A,B,C in R^2 such that f(A)=f(B)=f(C)=c and A,B,C are noncollinear.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply Lemma L4 directly to the given coloring f.

steps.derives: For the color c obtained in step A1, the set S_c = {P in R^2 : f(P)=c} is closed under circumcenters of noncollinear triples of its points.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conclusion of Lemma L1 applied to f and the chosen color c.

steps.derives: The points A,B,C from step A1 all belong to S_c, and they are noncollinear.
steps.trivial_justification: By definition of S_c, the equalities f(A)=f(B)=f(C)=c imply A,B,C are elements of S_c; noncollinearity was part of step A1.

Lemma L5 applies because step A2 gives the required circumcenter-closure property for S_c, and step A3 provides a noncollinear triple of points lying in S_c. Therefore every point of R^2 belongs to S_c.

steps.derives: For every point P in R^2, f(P)=c.
steps.trivial_justification: Since S_c = R^2 and S_c was defined as {P : f(P)=c}, every point P lies in S_c, hence f(P)=c.

steps.derives: There exists a color c in {red,green} such that for every point P in R^2, f(P)=c.
steps.trivial_justification: Step A5 exhibits the required witness c and proves the universal statement for that c.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let f : R^2 -> {red,green} be a coloring of the Euclidean plane. Assume that for every noncollinear triple of points A,B,C in R^2, if f(A)=f(B)=f(C), then f(circumcenter(A,B,C)) = f(A). Fix a color c in {red,green}, and define S_c = {P in R^2 : f(P)=c}. Then S_c has the following closure property: whenever A,B,C are noncollinear points of S_c, the point circumcenter(A,B,C) also belongs to S_c.

candidates.strategy_summary: Reduce the coloring statement to a structural theorem about a single color class viewed as a subset of the plane that is closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples. Then prove that some color class must contain a noncollinear triple, and invoke the structural theorem to conclude that this color class is the whole plane.
